Consult Summary:
- 19-year-old woman with 3 days of dysuria and lower abdominal cramping, small amount of visible blood in urine earlier today; clinician impression: likely uncomplicated urinary tract infection (bladder infection) with plan for short-course oral antibiotics, hydration, and follow-up if not improved.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - Pain with urination (burning/stinging) for a few days.
  - Lower abdominal crampy pain concurrent with urination.
  - Noted a small amount of blood in urine earlier today.
  - Urine described as having an unusual odor.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms started "a few days" ago and are ongoing; not improved with over-the-counter bicarbonate taken a couple of days ago.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Symptoms occur with micturition; bicarbonate did not relieve symptoms.
  - Patient advised to increase fluids (plan) to help relieve symptoms.
- Associated symptoms:
  - No increased urinary frequency reported.
  - No nausea, vomiting.
  - No fever.
  - No back or flank pain.
  - No abnormal vaginal discharge reported.
- Systems review / pertinent negatives:
  - Bowel function reported as normal; no diarrhea.
  - Denies fevers, chills, vomiting, flank pain, or other systemic symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- Irritable bowel syndrome (patient-reported).
- No other chronic medical conditions reported.
- Family history: no known kidney, bladder, bowel, or gut conditions reported.

Medications:
- No regular prescription medications reported.
- Took over-the-counter bicarbonate a couple of days ago for symptom relief (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Antibiotic options discussed and to be prescribed: nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim — plan described as a three-day course, one tablet twice daily (dose/route not documented).
Allergies:
- Clindamycin — causes swelling when taken (patient report). Clinician characterized as a significant allergy (per transcript).

Social History:
- Lives in a flat near college with friends.
- Student (studying biology).
- Tobacco: denies smoking.
- Alcohol: drinks socially on weekends.
- Sexual activity: sexually active with a boyfriend for a couple of months; uses condoms as contraception.
- No other substance use or financial/lifestyle issues documented.

Family History:
- No relevant family history of renal, bladder, bowel disease reported.

Physical Examination:
- No vital signs documented.
- No physical examination findings documented; clinician stated intention to proceed to examination but none performed during this consult.

Investigations:
- No investigations performed during this consult.
- Patient has never had an STD screen (patient report).
- Clinician recommended pregnancy testing if concern for pregnancy.
- No urinalysis, urine dipstick, urine culture, or STI tests documented.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis)
  - Assessment: Clinical diagnosis of likely simple UTI based on dysuria, lower abdominal discomfort, malodorous urine, and brief episode of visible blood.
  - Plan:
    - Offer antibiotic therapy: either nitrofurantoin or trimethoprim; plan described as a three-day course, one tablet twice daily (dose/route not documented).
    - Advise increased oral fluids to help flush the urinary tract.
    - Suggest cranberry juice may help symptomatically.
    - Advise avoidance of sexual intercourse while symptomatic; continue barrier contraception if used.
    - Provide safety-netting: return or call if symptoms worsen or if new fever, back/flank pain, or systemic illness develops (concern for possible upper tract infection/pyelonephritis).
    - If symptoms not improved by end of the week, contact clinic for reassessment.
- Issue 2: Reproductive/sexual health considerations
  - Assessment: Sexually active without prior STD screening; pregnancy unlikely per patient but not definitively excluded.
  - Plan:
    - Recommend pregnancy test if there is any concern.
    - Consider STI screening if clinically indicated or if symptoms persist/worsen.
- Issue 3: Medication allergy
  - Assessment: Reported allergy to clindamycin with swelling.
  - Plan:
    - Avoid clindamycin; document allergy in medication/allergy list.
- General plan items:
  - No physical exam or point-of-care testing performed in this consult; clinician planned to examine but did not during the call.
  - Follow-up arranged if no improvement by end of week or earlier if worsening symptoms.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure).
  - Physical examination findings (abdominal, costovertebral angle, genital/pelvic exam).
  - Urinalysis/urine dipstick and urine culture results.
  - Pregnancy test result.
  - STI screen status/results.
  - Specific antibiotic choice/dose in mg and route, and explicit prescription documentation.
  - Documentation of contraception beyond barrier use (e.g., partner status, method consistency).
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - None clinically significant identified. (Clinician restated timing of last period as "three weeks ago" while patient stated "a couple of weeks ago" — minor discrepancy; conflict noted.)
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall audible and clear; occasional brief inaudible words but sufficient information to form assessment and plan.
